source_name: Banka Slovenije – Primerjava stroškov bančnih storitev za potrošnike / prebivalstvo (bank fee comparison series)
why_relevant: Recurring (roughly semi-annual) bank-by-bank price comparison of a basket of payment services, including card issuance and maintenance fees, ATM withdrawal charges and account packages. Gives per-institution pricing that no aggregate statistic exposes — directly relevant to competitive analysis of card/ATM economics.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Seznam notifikacij plačilnih institucij (PDF notification list)
why_relevant: Periodically republished PDF listing notifications received from home-state competent authorities for payment institutions serving Slovenia. Dated filenames make it a good longitudinal series for tracking inbound market entry.

source_name: Banka Slovenije coverage of ECB studies (Slovenian-language gateway to SPACE)
why_relevant: The NCB's Slovenian-language write-up of the ECB SPACE results is the only place euro-area cash-study findings are rendered with explicit Slovenian framing and local terminology; it is also the practical entry point for sl-language discovery of ECB material (ECB itself publishes SPACE/PSS almost exclusively in English).

source_name: SURS — Anketa o porabi v gospodinjstvih (APG / Household Budget Survey)
why_relevant: Detailed household expenditure structure by category, plus savings and indebtedness and durable-goods equipment. Underpins CPI weights and gives the spending basket against which payment-instrument use is normalised.

source_name: SURS methodological explanations and quality reports (Metodološka pojasnila / Poročila o kakovosti)
why_relevant: Defines exactly what each indicator covers, break-in-series dates (e.g. COICOP 1999 to COICOP 2018 switch), sample design and known quality limitations. Essential to avoid mis-normalising payment data against a redefined denominator.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — annual reports (Letno poročilo) PDFs
why_relevant: Audited annual reports of the domestic processor contain revenue, transaction/processing volumes, number of cards and terminals processed, ownership shares of member banks, and business commentary on the SI card market. The 2019 report explicitly compares Bankart-processed POS count against Bank of Slovenia totals — a rare direct market-share datapoint.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. annual reports (letno poročilo) — vendor and ATM-fleet disclosures
why_relevant: Bankart's annual reports name the ATM makes in the managed fleet (NCR, Wincor Nixdorf, Diebold, Diebold Nixdorf) and describe processing volumes and platform projects. Because Bankart processes for most SI banks, this is the closest thing to an aggregate ATM/POS estate inventory, and it doubles as a vendor-mapping source.

source_name: Slovenian IT/business trade press covering bank innovation (Racunalniske novice, Svet kapitala, Delo Podjetnistvo)
why_relevant: Trade press reports hackathon outcomes, award placements and bank innovation programmes with participant counts and prize funds, and frequently quotes bank executives giving numbers not in official releases. Useful weak-signal amplifier and a route to discovering events that were never announced on a corporate site.

source_name: Delo / Finance — Slovenian business press coverage of interchange and card fees
why_relevant: National business press is where SI-specific interchange/MDR disputes, Bankart ownership changes and acquirer entries surface first, often quoting figures not otherwise published. The archived Delo piece on IFR caps and Slovenia is an example of usable local commentary.

source_name: ECB payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, e.g. first half of 2025)
why_relevant: Narrative + tables accompanying each semi-annual payments-statistics release; gives release calendar, revisions notes and headline euro-area context in which the SI row must be read.

source_name: ECB SPACE 2024 statistical annexes (Annex A/B country tables)
why_relevant: Country-by-country breakdowns (payment shares by instrument, value bands, P2P, online, cash access/acceptance perceptions) where the Slovenia column lives. This is the extractable layer, not the narrative report.

entity_name: Javna agencija RS za varstvo konkurence
source_name: AVK — letna poročila (annual reports)
why_relevant: Annual report enumerates cases opened/closed by sector, including consumer-credit and financial-services analyses covering named banks, branches and savings banks; gives caseload counts and sectoral focus that indicate where competition pressure on fees is being examined.

source_name: Združenje Povezani smo — cash-rights advocacy association
why_relevant: Civil-society association that collected 56,000+ signatures (2023) for a constitutional right to use cash, culminating in a National Assembly constitutional amendment (reported 67–1) enshrining the right to use cash in banking and legal transactions. Materially changes the SI cash-access policy environment — a hard constraint on branch/ATM rationalisation and on any cashless-acceptance strategy. Caveat: an activist body with unrelated campaigns; treat as an actor, not as a data source, and corroborate.

entity_name: Bank general terms & conditions archives as evidence exhibits
source_name: Bank general terms & conditions archives as evidence exhibits (e.g. Intesa Sanpaolo Bank SI, SKB, Gorenjska banka)
why_relevant: Splošni pogoji documents are the artefacts that consumer bodies, inspectors and courts adjudicate; they state ADR routes, fee-change mechanics and card liability rules. Useful as the raw comparison base against ZPS/BS fee comparisons and ADR opinions.

source_name: Deloitte Slovenija — Digital Banking Maturity 2020 (SI-language page)
why_relevant: Slovenian-language write-up of the DBM study with SI-specific commentary (4,900 customers surveyed, 19 scenarios, SI banks ranked as digital laggards). Local-language framing often names SI banks and channels not in the regional English deck.

source_name: NLB Group corporate pages on Bankart (ownership/role disclosure)
why_relevant: Bank-side page describing Bankart's role in processing modern payment instruments for the group and market. Anchors the vendor-route analysis: it establishes the ownership/commercial link that makes Bankart's supplier choices binding on most SI banks' card and ATM estates.

source_name: NLB Hackathon 'Odprte finance' – press releases and results
why_relevant: Hackathon briefs state what the bank considers its open-banking/API problem set, and the results release names winning solution themes (financial literacy, PSD2 aggregation). Challenge statements are an unusually candid statement of internal priorities and API capability, published before any product launch.

source_name: OZS - Obrtno-podjetniska zbornica Slovenije (Chamber of Craft and Small Business) - ZDUPS consultation response
why_relevant: The small-business chamber is the merchant-side stakeholder in the cash debate: its members both accept cash (and therefore need deposit access and CIT services) and would be obliged under ZDUPS to accept at least one electronic payment method. Its consultation commentary and zastopanje (advocacy) pages capture merchant complaints about cash deposit costs, branch closures affecting daily takings, and card acceptance costs - the merchant-facing half of the cash-access ecosystem that bank-side sources omit.

source_name: Slovenian media coverage of bank IT platform migrations (BKS Bank platform switch fallout)
why_relevant: When a vendor/platform migration fails publicly, SI media describe the systems involved in detail (BKS Bank SI moved core banking and payments onto the Austrian parent's new platform; duplicate direct debits, wrong statements, Flik issues). Failure reporting is one of the few routes that dates and names bank platform changes in local language.

source_name: Zveza potrošnikov Slovenije / consumer-advocacy mystery-shopping studies (via RTV SLO coverage)
why_relevant: Independent mystery-shopping research on SI banks' basic payment accounts — reveals distribution/access practice and per-bank behaviour that no statistical series captures. Indirect: reveals market conduct rather than reporting volumes.

source_name: Slovenian business press coverage of bank results (Vecer, Forbes Slovenija/N1, Zurnal24)
why_relevant: Results coverage frequently quotes figures banks state in briefings but do not publish in a machine-readable form (e.g. 'largest branch/ATM network in Slovenia', ~450 shared ATMs, profit and revenue splits). Useful as an early signal and as a pointer to the underlying press release, but must always be traced back to the primary report.

entity_name: Academic and student theses on cash transport and ATM security in Slovenia
source_name: Academic and student theses on cash transport and ATM security in Slovenia (e.g. academia.si diploma on comparison of cash transport and protection)
why_relevant: Slovenian diploma and masters theses on private security routinely compare CIT providers, describe operational practice, and reproduce operator-supplied data (fleet sizes, route economics, ATM servicing frequency) that companies will not disclose to a researcher directly. They also cite the regulatory framework precisely. Combined with the national repository, this is an underrated route to CIT operational detail. The national aggregator repozitorij.uni-lj.si / dKUM and the Univerza v Mariboru Faculty of Criminal Justice output should be swept alongside this single example.

entity_name: Bankart corporate profile deck hosted by ŠC Kranj
source_name: Bankart corporate profile deck hosted by ŠC Kranj (third-party mirror)
why_relevant: A company-presentation PDF (prepared for a school career/industry event) mirrored on a third-party education site. Such recruitment-event decks carry operational volume figures and org detail that the corporate site trims, and they survive on the host long after the company withdraws them — an accidental archive.

source_name: Deloitte CEE M&A Banking Study (annual)
why_relevant: Annual Deloitte study of CEE banking consolidation with per-country chapters; the SI chapter tracks market concentration (NLB, OTP acquisitions), asset shares and competitive structure — context for card/acquiring market share shifts.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf investor press releases — Bankart / Vynamic Transaction Middleware
why_relevant: Vendor press release (13 May 2024) discloses that Bankart, Slovenia's dominant card/payment processor, is replacing its legacy Base24 platform with Diebold Nixdorf Vynamic Transaction Middleware, serving ATMs, POS and e-commerce for ~20 banks in six SEE countries. Quantifies estate scope and switch-migration timing — exactly the procurement detail that is otherwise invisible.

source_name: European Court of Auditors — Special Report 01/2025 'Digital payments in the EU'
why_relevant: Independent audit of EU digital-payments policy; audits typically expose data gaps, supervisory weaknesses and member-state comparisons that are not visible in ECB statistics, and cite underlying datasets useful for snowballing.

source_name: Humanfrog — case study: Sberbank banka (Slovenia)
why_relevant: Small SI digital agency publishing a named bank case study (Sberbank banka, the SI entity later absorbed into NLB as N Banka). Illustrates the long tail of small vendors that name SI bank clients — useful for digital-channel and campaign-side intelligence and for reconstructing the Sberbank→N Banka→NLB transition.

source_name: Kansas City Fed — Credit and Debit Card Interchange Fees in Various Countries (annual update)
why_relevant: Annual cross-country compendium that includes Slovenia's interchange caps/regime; a stable, citable secondary benchmark when scheme PDFs are hard to pin down, and a good consistency check on IFR implementation.

entity_name: Letno porocilo 2024 OTP Skupine Slovenija in OTP banke d.d.
source_name: Letno porocilo 2024 OTP Skupine Slovenija in OTP banke d.d. (full PDF)
why_relevant: First post-merger annual report for the combined OTP Slovenia group; the single document containing the consolidated branch/ATM/card figures for the merged bank. Mirrored on a third-party site, which is itself useful as a fallback when the bank's own path rotates.

source_name: Logate — case study: NLB Banka Podgorica (CX360)
why_relevant: Regional vendor case study on an NLB Group subsidiary. NLB Group standardises platforms across markets, so subsidiary-level vendor references are a leading indicator of what may be rolled into the Slovenian parent — a classic indirect route into an otherwise opaque group procurement.

source_name: Mastercard Masterindex — Slovenian payment-habits consumer survey
why_relevant: The recurring branded consumer survey on Slovenian payment habits (card penetration ~90%+, weekly card use, contactless perception, mobile-app payment share, cash-retention preference). No public body produces this attitudinal series; results are released via SI media and industry bodies rather than a stable Mastercard page.

source_name: Nets (Nexi Group) / Bankart instant-payments infrastructure announcement (FinTech Futures coverage)
why_relevant: Documents that Nets deployed and operates the RealTime24/7 instant-payments solution behind Bankart's national SCT/SCT Inst infrastructure — i.e. the technology supplier under Slovenia's instant-payment (Flik) rails. Key for understanding who controls SI payment-statistics-generating infrastructure.

source_name: SKB banka letna porocila archive (skb.si) — pre-merger baseline
why_relevant: SKB's last standalone annual reports (through FY2023) hold the pre-merger branch count, ATM fleet and Visa card portfolio that the merged OTP entity absorbed. Essential for building a continuous series across the merger break; the domain may be retired, so archive early.

source_name: Stripe – Payments in Slovenia market guide
why_relevant: PSP-authored country guide summarising merchant-relevant acceptance facts (card share of POS transaction value and count, contactless penetration, preferred local methods). Convenient orientation layer for the merchant acceptance mix, though derived from third-party data and commercially framed.

source_name: Temenos success stories — Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB)
why_relevant: Vendor case study documenting Temenos core at NLB since 2002 (corporate first, then retail, incl. N Banka retail migration) with quantified claims (time-to-market -50%, onboarding +20% faster, multicurrency accounts). Establishes NLB's core-banking dependency and upgrade cadence, plus the N Banka integration timeline.

source_name: Wikipedija (sl) — Sistem Activa
why_relevant: Compact Slovenian-language history and structure of the Activa card system (founded 1992 at Banka Koper; clearing by Intesa Sanpaolo, settlement by Banka Slovenije via TARGET2-Slovenija; covers Mastercard/Visa/Activa/Maestro/Cirrus/Visa Electron). Useful for glossary and actor-map seeding, not as evidence.

source_name: ZBS Bančna konferenca – recorded sessions on YouTube
why_relevant: Full recordings of the annual ZBS banking conference (2023, 2024 editions found). Spoken remarks and presentation slides frequently contain volume figures, cash-usage commentary and project timelines that never appear in written form — a classic weak-signal and last-resort recovery channel.
